question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Under JTB Knowledge = JTB and any non-Knowledge attitude is just Belief. That leaves no place for the two mixed cases that are made by crossing J/¬J with T/¬T.

* Justified False Belief. A belief p can be justified and false. It is not JTB, so on the two-state taxonomy it can only be Belief. Belief is therefore used for a justified attitude that is epistemically respectable but false. The category Belief is thereby forced to contain both justified and unjustified false attitudes and we lose a principled way to say that a justified false belief is epistemically better than an unjustified false belief.

* Unjustified True Belief. A belief p can be true and unjustified. It is not JTB, so on the two-state taxonomy it can only be Belief. Belief is therefore used for a true attitude that is epistemically defective. The category Belief is thereby forced to contain both true and false, justified and unjustified attitudes and we lose a principled way to say that a true belief is epistemically better than a false belief.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief the residue category Belief is heterogeneous: it is the disjunction J¬T ∨ ¬J T ∨ ¬J ¬T, i.e. justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief all lumped together. JTB cannot mark the epistemic difference between a justified false belief and a merely false belief, nor between an unjustified true belief and a merely false belief, so justification and truth are lost as independent dimensions of epistemic appraisal once the two states are exhausted.

2.text:
With JTB knowledge is the intersection of Truth and Justification.

T  J   = Knowledge
T ¬J  = true belief without justification
F  J   = justified false belief
F ¬J  = false belief without justification

If Belief is the only residual epistemic category left besides Knowledge then everything that is not JTB has to be put into Belief. That forces two collapses.

* Justified false belief has no home. It is not Knowledge because it is not True, and on the usual reading Belief is the un-justified/un-knowledgeable state. A justified false belief is epistemically better than a mere, unjustified false belief - it is the product of good evidence, good method, etc. - but on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it is lumped with mere false belief under Belief, or is left unclassifiable altogether. That is the epistemic value without truth case.

* Unjustified true belief is lumped with false belief. An unjustified true belief is not Knowledge because it is not Justified, and so it goes into the Belief bin together with unjustified false belief. Truth is thereby eclipsed: a lucky true belief and a plain false belief receive the same epistemic label, Belief, even though one is true and the other is false. That is the epistemic luck / truth without justification case.

In particular the taxonomy cannot distinguish justified false belief from unjustified false belief, nor unjustified true belief from unjustified false belief, so the epistemic differences between justification and truth are lost once Knowledge = Justified True Belief is taken as exhaustive.

F ¬J = unjustified false belief

Truth is lost as an independent dimension of appraisal; a lucky true belief receives the same label as a false belief, eclipsing epistemic luck.
